followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the formal Loyada asylum-admission/reception restriction, whose origin predates the observation window but is explicitly discussed in an October 2017 UNHCR submission. The evidence concerns asylum-seekers arriving from Somalia into Djibouti through the formal reception route. Informal arrivals continued. It does not establish closure to every traveller or all goods. Retain May 2014 month bounds, unknown endpoint and no day-specific last-confirmation date. The October 2017 document date stays in text, without inventing an observation day or a continuous numeric duration. No operational complete/exact flags or daily animation interval are created. The security/armed-attacks rationale follows UNHCR’s account of the May 2014 attack. An affected asylum cohort does not by itself support migration control as an additional official purpose. The UNHCR submission and its October date were freshly inspected. The 2014 UNHCR account remains a cached indexed extract, and both reports share the institutional origin. OSM records are coordinate evidence only. The approved approximate point matches saved OSM node 8405526244 at 11.4602871 / 43.2569738; nearby way 778712166 names the Djibouti–Somalia border post. This does not locate every informal route or prove historical operation. Policy-only display remains constrained by the lack of an in-window observation day.

Correct the WHO cargo attribution and Kamanyola source paraphrase; preserve the original error and rejected formula overwrite transparently. The eight programme additions require no factual changes. Keep all source-access, reporting-origin, geography, directional, policy/operational and uncertain-duration qualifications. Completion describes the audit procedure for this sample, not proof that unknown attributes or every database record are verified.
